checkpoints.title: CLI and ready package: aayu ready <story> makes a Story Ready only while its Feature's Approve to build covers it. ready.Ready gains Covered, which only Apply runs, after the issue passes, on the same read the snapshot freezes; Check and Guard never call it, so the Ready guard and build --next (which use Check) never remove a Ready granted before the rule. storyCovered refuses with exit 4 and writes nothing when the Story has no parent Feature, the Feature has no specs/<f>/approved.json (unless specs/<f>/approved-early-<s>.json of #994 covers this one story at its body hash), a part of the Feature was approved again or its intent, tech, or UX pins drifted after the approval (spec drift is left to the per-story check), or the story's Completion Goal hash, effort, or title differs from the approval, or the story is not in it. The refusals name aayu ready <f> or aayu ready <f> --ack <s>, as the criteria say; --ack itself is #877 S3, not this story. A covered story's snapshot gains the row Approved to build | #<f> approval <k> by @<login>
contracts: ready.Ready.Covered func(ctx, workitems.Item, body string) (row string, err error); nil keeps Ready as before
ready.Result.ApprovedToBuild string (json approved_to_build), rendered as the snapshot row Approved to build
ready.StoryOf(workitems.Item) ApprovedStory and ready.StoryChanges(was, now) []string; Approve to build pins stories with StoryOf too
cli: botReady returns Arjun's *ledger.Writer; the early-build record is read by path and schema aayudha.feature.early-build/v1 only
instrumentation: a refusal writes nothing; a covered Ready is the existing ledger commit and github.comment.ready-snapshot action, now naming the approval
checkpoints.rollback: revert the PR; aayu ready <story> makes a story Ready without reading the approval again, and snapshots already written keep their row

checkpoints.title: Skill: skills/ready/SKILL.md gains a section on the Story rule: what refuses a Story, that only the Completion Goal, effort, and title need an acknowledgment, the early build, that --check does not read the approval, and that the guard and build --next never apply the rule. No verb, flag, or seat changes, so no generated file changes
contracts: skills/ready/SKILL.md body only; the frontmatter is unchanged

checkpoints.title: Test fake: internal/github/fake lists every issue in number order, not only issues 1 to n, so the scenario's issue numbers (#700, #840, #851-#858) are listed. Production code is unchanged
contracts: fake GET /repos/<r>/issues iterates the sorted issue numbers
